title: Book 13 opens: still priesthood; Levites’ tithe-of-tithe to Aaron
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK THIRTEEN. Still concerning priesthood.

So then concerning priests and Aaron, let these things from us have been said for now. And I think one must bring near to what I said the things seeming to have been left out, at least the things legislated upon the Levites. For thus the word would have itself sufficient.
Palladius: So then go on, and speak clearly; for you think rightly.

Cyril: Setting then the best order upon the sacred-works, he sets under the high priest the Levitical rank, saying thus in Numbers: ‘And to the Levites you will speak, and you will say toward them: If you should take from the sons of Israel the tenth, which I have given you from them in a lot, you also will take away from it a taking-away to Lord, a tenth from the tenth, and your taking-aways will be reckoned for you as grain from a threshing-floor, and a taking-away from a winepress. Thus you also will take them away from all the taking-aways of Lord from all your tenths, as many as if you should take from the sons of Israel; and you will give from them a taking-away to Lord, to Aaron the priest from all your gifts you will take away a taking-away to Lord, or from all the firstfruits the sanctified from it. And you will say toward them: Whenever you take away the firstfruit from it, it will also be reckoned to the Levites as produce from a threshing-floor, and as produce from a winepress; and you will eat it in every place, you and your sons, and your houses, because this is a wage for you instead of your liturgies the in the tent of the witness; and you will not take sin through it, because if you should take away the firstfruit from it; and you will not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, in order that you may not’
translator_notes: Ends mid μὴ into §2 ἀποθάνητε; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Tithe typed Christ/Melchizedek; Levi separate census; given to Aaron
english: Cyril: …die.’ Do you see the mystery of Christ as still in shadows, and shining-before in types? For the one taking tenths has been tenthed, according to blessed Paul’s voice. But then at least the type in Melchizedek, and in times according to Moses has been kept again as in Aaron, the priest of the priests Christ signifying upon himself the leader, and set over the holy tent—that is the Church—the Holy of holies, and God of gods, to whom every fruit-bearing from us is owed. For it has been written that ‘All those around him will bring gifts.’ But the Mosaic things still in types, and now with spiritual fruit-bearings the genuine keepers of the Gospel ordinances make glad their own Redeemer.
Palladius: You spoke well.

Cyril: And that the Levitical race is chosen-out, and set apart from the others, he makes clear according to some such manner. He ordered the popular to be numbered, and an accurate reckoning of the herd multitude to be made—not with the Creator having been ignorant. For drops of rain have been numbered for him, according to what has been written, and nothing would escape the pure mind—but in order that those lighting upon the sacred Writings may know also very clearly that those lying upon God and having been named his people go in enrollments the with God, and in a book of life, and numbered among the known, and already in memories of the Master of all. So then the popular was being enrolled, and God was setting as it were apart the chosen-out and sacred race, and was not releasing it from somewhere in equal rank with the others, but was storing up for it as it were the outstanding share, saying toward Moses the all-wise: ‘See the tribe of Levi, you will not visit-together the number of them, and you will not take in midst of the sons of Israel.’ For exceptional is the lot of the saints, and in superiorities the prizes. And somehow also in other books is the enrollment; for all-divine Daniel has not beheld one, but as he himself says: ‘A tribunal sat, and books were opened.’ So then according to analogous measures of each is the enrollment. And the race distributed and dedicated to the divine sacred-works has been as it were set out from the other multitude, and straightway he was clarifying the manner of the Levites’ sacred-work saying: ‘Take the tribe of Levi, and you will set them opposite Aaron the priest, and they will liturgize for him, and they will keep his watches, and the watches of the sons of Israel before the tent of the witness, to work the works of the tent; and they will keep all the vessels of the tent of the witness, and the watches of the sons of Israel according to all the works of the tent. And you will give the Levites to Aaron your brother, and to his sons the priests; given as a gift these are to me from the sons of Israel, and Aaron and his sons you will set upon the tent of the witness. And they will keep their priesthood, and all the things according to the altar, and inside the veil; and the alien who touches will die.’ So then the
translator_notes: Ends mid Οἱ μὲν οὖν into §3 Λευῗται; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Levites coworkers; bishops/presbyters/deacons typed; separate Levi census
english: Cyril: …Levites have been distributed as somehow coworkers and as it were helpers for the sacred-workers, for they will keep his watches—clear that of Aaron—and all the vessels of the tent of the witness, and the keepings of the sons of Israel. And unto these is the manner of their coworking. And he sets upon the tent both Aaron and the sons with him, and ‘They will keep,’ he says, ‘their own priesthood and all according to the altar, and the inward of the veil,’ that is the unspeakable and more mystical things, and as many as it is custom for those sitting-near the divine altar to do; and purely as unto Christ is the type, whom the Father set upon his house, of which house we are. And not unclearly would those priesting-with Aaron mark the holy and admirable chorus of the holy apostles, as it were coworking and co-liturgizing with Christ. For they have become coworkers of God, stewards and managers of mysteries of God, and indeed also ministers, through whom we have believed. And if someone should choose also to investigate carefully the order of the Church, the pre-typing in law, he would reasonably marvel. For to bishops, as those allotted then to lead, and indeed to those managing upon the middle rank—presbyters I mean—the altar has been entrusted, and the things inside the veil, for whom it would also be fitting to be said: ‘And they will keep their priesthood’; and to deacons at least the, ‘They will keep the watches of the tent, and all its vessels, and the keepings of the people.’ Or do not they themselves order crying out in churches, sometimes that peoples must hymn what is fitting, and stand in good-order, and often be quiet, and they raise unto prayers, and with the bloodless sacrifice being finished, they themselves bring near the more sacred of the vessels, and make fine oversight upon all the necessary things?
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then those outstanding priest, and the Levites take-part-with of the order of the church priesthood, with the legal writing pre-voicing. And the popular is shut out from every sacred deed, and the word concerning the last things has been hung upon those snatching the honor. For he will die, he says, if some volunteer should come upon it, not having the divine vote upon himself.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: So then unarranged with the enrollments of the others is the Levitical, yet enrolled specially and in a book of God; ‘For the Lord spoke,’ he says, ‘toward Moses in the desert Sinai saying: Visit the sons of Levi according to houses of their patriarchies, according to their peoples, according to their kinships. Every male from a month-old and upward, visit them; and Moses and Aaron visited them through a voice of Lord, in which manner the Lord arranged for them. And these were the sons of Levi from their names, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari; these the names of the
translator_notes: Ends mid τῶν into §4 υἱῶν Γεδσών; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Month-old Levi = Christlike infancy; Kohath holy-of-holies coverings begin
english: Cyril: …sons of Gershon, according to their peoples, Libni and Shimei. And sons of Kohath according to their peoples, Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel; and sons of Merari according to their peoples, Mahli and Mushi. These are peoples of the Levites according to houses of their patriarchies.’ So then observe, O Palladius, and before the others that. For fine is the oversight. So then the popular was being enrolled from twenty-years and upward, the legal accuracy, I somehow think, not deeming worthy the still powerless and inactive, the also being written in a book of God. For the swelling and already in spiritual peaks would reasonably be judged into the catalogues of the saints. So then the law makes a well-natured under-typing of the spiritual age, the bodily, and was setting the in peaks as a chosen-out race, running past the under-age and weak, and still boyish, and not setting in a sacred book. But upon at least the Levites, from a month-old the enrollment has become; for the Master of all accepts also very gladly the infancy in Christ of those chosen-out, just as indeed the thoughtful. For to excel in both is exceptional, in understanding, I say, and simplicity the according to Christ. And indeed all-divine Paul: ‘Brothers, do not become children in the minds, but in the badness be infant, and in the minds become perfect.’ And somewhere Christ himself also says: ‘Become thoughtful as the snakes, and unmixed as the doves.’ So then acceptable is the simplicity of the saints. And by name and indeed also by peoples and patriarchies is the visiting. For God deems worthy of own oversight whomsoever he should choose to honor, both according to one, and according to multitude, and according to race. And the accurate at least in these, the Savior himself will clarify saying to the holy apostles: ‘Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion, and one of them will not fall upon the earth without your Father the in the heavens? And of you even all the hairs of the head have been numbered.’
Palladius: You spoke well.

Cyril: And beside this he was further legislating a second enrollment of the Levitical people to be made, and that for each the liturgy fitting him must have been ordered, saying ‘Take the head-count of the sons of Kohath from midst of sons of Levi, according to their peoples, according to houses of their patriarchies, from twenty and five years, and upward until fifty years, everyone going in to liturgize to do all the works in the tent of the witness. And these the works of the sons of Kohath in the tent of the witness, Holy of holies. And Aaron and his sons will go in, whenever the camp should lift, and will take down the veil the overshadowing, and will cover in it the ark of the witness. And they will set upon it a covering of hyacinth skin, and will cast upon it a whole hyacinth garment from above, and will put through the carrying-poles, and upon the table the set-forward they will cast upon it a whole-purple garment, and the bowls, and the censers, and the cups, and the drink-offering vessels in which they pour, and the breads which will continually upon it
translator_notes: Ends mid ἔσον into §5 ται; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Kohath covers holy things; age 25–50 = strong mind; hyacinth = from-heaven
english: Cyril: …be, and they will cast upon it a scarlet garment, and will cover it with a covering of hyacinth skin, and will put through it the carrying-poles. And they will take a hyacinth garment, and will cover the lampstand the lighting, and its lamps, and its tongs, and its snuffers, and all the vessels of the oil, with which they liturgize in them. And they will put it, and all its vessels, into a covering of hyacinth skin, and will set it upon carrying-poles, and upon the golden altar they will cover over a hyacinth garment, and will cover it with a covering of hyacinth skin, and will put through its carrying-poles, and will take all the liturgical vessels as many as they liturgize in them in the holy things, and will put into a hyacinth garment, and will cover them with a covering of hyacinth skin, and will set upon carrying-poles, and will set the cover upon the altar, and will cover over it a whole-purple garment, and will set upon it all the vessels with which they liturgize upon it in them, and the fire-pans, and the flesh-hooks, and the bowls, and the cover, and all the vessels of the altar, and will cast upon it a covering of hyacinth skin, and will put through its carrying-poles. And they will take a purple garment, and will cover-together the laver and its base, and will put it into a covering of hyacinth skin, and will set upon carrying-poles, and Aaron and his sons will finish, covering the holy things, and all the holy vessels, in the lifting of the camp and after these the sons of Kohath will go in to lift, and will not touch the holy things, in order that they may not die.’ So then the enrollment from month-olds also teaches that the very harmlessness of the saints is pleasing and well-acceptable to God. And that only the age defined by the law—the from twenty-five, and until fifty years—has been distributed to the sacred works, that I think makes clear, that every as much as is already both thoughtful and well-strong finishes for God the exceptional liturgy and having it unreproachably. For already in these is the one become in twenty and five years, and still also the one having gone forward until fifty. For somehow already a man having driven beyond the fiftieth has nodded toward a leaving-off of strength, and is no longer in the blameless peaks, but creeps as it were upon the sufferings from old-age. And no one unwise, nor indeed powerless, would liturgize blamelessly for God, if at least it is true to say that works of strength and of a very beautiful mind would be as many as would look toward virtue; and it has been allotted that they must be praised by the lawgiver.
Palladius: Thus I say.

Cyril: And liturgy for those from people of Kohath, the Holy of holies, with the priests running-before and packing them. For everywhere more honorable is the outstanding in order, and all as many as are in good-order with God, and nothing altogether unordered. And the Levitical in under-services, and having been spread under the sacred-works of those overlying. And both with skins and hyacinth garments are packed the holy ark, and the gol
translator_notes: Ends mid χρυ into §6 σοῦν θυμιατήριον; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Hyacinth/purple/scarlet types; Gershon/Merari wagons; Kohath shoulders
english: Cyril: …den censer, and lampstand again and the liturgical vessels, the hyacinth signaling for us the from-above and from heaven. For such-colored is the from-above and unto depth aether. And that the sacred vessels are types of Christ the from-above and from heaven has already been shown-forth for us through long words beforehand. And the table has also a whole-purple garment toward the hyacinth wraps; and at least the altar of the fruitings, a scarlet garment, and indeed also the laver, a whole-purple garment upon the hyacinth packings. And the table, having the setting-forward of the breads, signals the bloodless sacrifice, through which we are blessed eating the bread from heaven, that is Christ, who also has become according to us, but was and is even thus God coming from-above and from Father, and above all as king and Lord of the wholes. And a riddle of the kingdom of Christ would be, as at least it appears to me, the purple garment having been stretched upon the table, or the purple wrap. And this altar of the fruitings was clothed with a scarlet garment; and we will accept the scarlet-dyed garment as a type of blood. For Christ has been sacrificed through us and over us, and as some lamb has gone up upon the divine altar, unto a smell of fragrance to God and Father. And toward the hyacinths, a whole-purple garment the curtain for the laver. And the laver writes upon itself the type of the holy baptism, washing us with holy waters unto putting-away of sin, and carrying off unto the kingdom of the heavens. And from-above and from heaven is the holy baptism; and a riddle of this, the hyacinth color. Or do I not seem to you to say these things best, as at least in such hard-to-grasp of contemplations?
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then such a liturgy for those from Kohath; and Gershonites again and indeed also Merarites, according to the equal manner, were being enrolled from twenty and five years and until fifty, by name according to houses and patriaries; and liturgy for the people of Gershon, the skins of the tent, the coverings, the hangings of the doors, and the sails of the court and the leftovers; and it has been written thus. And at least that from Merari (and this also a Levitical people), the pillars of the tent, the bases, the capitals, both pegs and bars, and the veil of the tent the outer, and some other things beside these. And those from Gershon and Merari were carrying through everywhere the things entrusted to themselves with the under-services through wagons. And Kohathites at least were going having the Holy of holies upon shoulders. For it has been written thus in Numbers: ‘And the rulers of Israel brought twelve rulers of houses of their patriarchies; these the rulers of tribes, these the ones having stood upon the oversight, and they brought their gifts before Lord, six covered wagons and twelve oxen. A wagon from two rulers,
translator_notes: Ends mid ἀρχόντων, into §7 καὶ μόσχον; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Wagons for extras; shoulders for Christ-types; law surplus vs Gospel holy
english: Cyril: …and a calf from each, and they brought opposite the tent. And the Lord said toward Moses, saying: Take from them, and they will be toward the liturgical works of the tent of the witness, and you will give them to the Levites, to each according to his liturgy. And Moses taking the wagons and the oxen, gave them to the Levites. And the two wagons and the four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon according to their liturgies, and the four wagons and the eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari according to their liturgies, through Ithamar son of Aaron the priest; and to the sons of Kohath he has not given, because they have the liturgies of the holy, upon shoulders they will lift.’ Do you hear how for some the custom is to lead and carry upon wagons, and for Kohathites alone, the sacred things unto shoulders?
Palladius: For the sake of what then?

Cyril: For somehow always in greater sweat is the outstanding and more sacred, and there follows it wholly and entirely the needing to labor, and beside this indeed, the enduring-suffering, and not in equal with the others, whoever should be both more holy, and somehow nearer rather to God. Or is what I say not true?
Palladius: Very much so.
Cyril: So then in such good-order the Levitical race was liturgizing. And I at least think the matter fills a type of a mystery.
Palladius: How then do you say?

Cyril: For the two peoples, Gershon and Merari, seem to under-hint the peoples in law, I mean Israel; and Kohathites at least, those sanctified in Christ through faith. For for some there was in care the sails of the court, the skins of the tent, the coverings and the pillars, both heads and bases, both pegs and stretchings-around, and as the sacred Writing says, ‘All the leftovers,’ through which the not-necessary of the liturgy is signaled. And those were emboldened to carry the Holy of holies, and the things through which Christ, not according to one manner, but rather many-ways and many-formedly is signaled, as ark, as table, and as golden lampstand, and golden censer. For being simple according to nature as God, he is known many-manneredly by the difference of the working. For agreedly living and energetic is the Word of the Father, and beside this life, and light, and smell of intelligible fragrance. So then as many as sit-near the commands through Moses have as liturgy the leftovers of the tent; for unhelpful is the law, unless it should be thought spiritually. And as many as have been emboldened for the Holy of holies are somehow wholly holy in Christ, leftover nothing, but as it were having Emmanuel himself as rider.
Palladius: You spoke well.
Cyril: And observe, if it seems good, also this.
Palladius: What then do you say?

Cyril: For those entrusted with the leftovers of the holy tent carry upon wagons. And Kohathites, the Holy of holies not upon wagons, not upon some other altogether, but having set upon the shoulders themselves were going.
translator_notes: Ends mid ᾔεσαν. into §8 dialogue; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Law a hard yoke; Christ’s light burden; first/last peoples; Korah begins
english: Palladius: What then is this at least?

Cyril: That, O companion, I would say, burdensome is the law, and a hard-to-bear load; and a clear indication of such would become, the leftovers not being carried unto shoulders, through at least the yoked being weak. Therefore also the all-divine disciples were saying to those going after the faith unto legal worship: ‘And now why do you test God, to set a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither you nor your fathers were strong to bear?’ And Kohathites, having set upon their own shoulders the things through which Christ is signaled, make a light and well-portable load. So then is this not clearly what Christ himself said: ‘My yoke is kind, and my load light’?
Palladius: It seems so.

Cyril: And I would still add to the things said also this. For it would not be unhelpful unto full-assurance; for in the first enrollment of the Levites, those from Gershon had been ranked in beginnings, then middle Kohath, and last Merari (and these Levitical peoples); and in the second, the from twenty and five years, Kohath has been set toward of the others, and has been named first. And last after him, Gershon and Merari, having as liturgy the leftovers of the tent. And each of these two peoples have only up to two patriaries, and the one goes forward even until four. So then do you understand the riddle?
Palladius: Least at least.

Cyril: For Israel has been called in firsts; and with the herd of the nations having run-in between, he has been ranked after this; and the lasts have become firsts, according to the Savior’s voice, and the firsts lasts.
Palladius: True.
Cyril: And that short in number of the Jews is the people, with the unmeasured multitude from nations overlying by much, is clear.
Palladius: For how not?

Cyril: Therefore God says toward hierophant Moses: ‘And now leave me, and having been angered I will consume-out this synagogue, and I will make you unto a great nation, and much more than this.’ So then with such liturgies the whole Levitical band has been honored; and a bound for them of the sacred-work to be yoked to the outstanding, and to do under hand the of Aaron. And at least to think over this and to seek the better of the things distributed to him and defined by God, was being shown through the trial itself as procurer of penalty and destruction. And it has been written again in Numbers: ‘And Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, spoke, and Dathan, and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On, son of Peleth, son of Reuben, and they stood up opposite Moses, and men of the sons of Israel fifty and two hundred, leaders of synagogue called-together of counsel, and named men stood-together upon Moses and Aaron, and said toward them: Let it be enough for you that
translator_notes: Ends mid ὅτι into §9 πᾶσα ἡ συναγωγή; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Korah: all holy?; earth swallows; keep allotted measure
english: Cyril: …all the synagogue, all are holy, and in them Lord; and why do you stand-down upon the synagogue of Lord?’ And Moses hearing, fell upon face, and spoke toward Korah and toward all his synagogue, saying: ‘God has visited and known those being his and the holy, and has brought near toward himself; and whom he chose for himself, he has brought near toward himself. Do this, take for yourselves fire-pans, Korah and all his synagogue, and set fire upon them, and set incense upon them before Lord tomorrow; and the man whom Lord has chosen, this one holy; let it be enough for you, sons of Levi.’ And Moses said toward Korah: ‘Hear me, sons of Levi. Is this small for you, that God of Israel has set you apart from synagogue of Israel, and has brought you near toward himself to liturgize the liturgies of the tent of Lord, and to stand before the tent to serve him, and has brought you near and all your brothers sons of Levi with you, and you seek to priest?’ For those from Kohath having as liturgy the lifting unto shoulders the Holy of holies, were leaping-upon mindlessly the overlying and contending with the measures of the priests. For snatching for themselves the honors, according to what has been written, and having neglected the divine command, and running over unholily laws of the sacred-work, deeming the honors of those set-over of altogether little word. For they were saying toward Moses and Aaron: ‘Let it be enough for you that all the synagogue, all are holy, and in them Lord.’ Do you hear how they dishonor the measure distributed to themselves, only not saying the honor of the high priest is common, and not for the same peoples, but also for all the others, and nothing at all the surplus, or more manifest, even if they should be said to overlie having obtained the matter by a vote the from God; which is clearly to blame the votes from above, and to reckon as nothing what seems good to the lawgiver. But all-divine Moses, using the accustomed gentleness, was calling-alongside as having been sickened, and having thought-through the anger about to be according to them as much as not yet, rebukes saying: ‘Let it be enough for you, the sons of Levi. For not small,’ he says, ‘for you, that from all the God of the wholes has made you chosen-out toward the thus solemn and admirable liturgy.’ And they were still bitter and hard, and unbridled toward disdain, until the things of the madness had stepped into such an evil for them, that the earth having opened the mouth took them with races and tents, and wrapped with a strange destruction. For they went down into Hades living, according to what has been written. So then unholy and having a writing of death with God is the standing-down against a head, and the not yielding to those pre-ordered, and those having obtained the outstanding honor from God. And a fruit of the uppermost understanding is to be solemn and give-thanks upon whatever one should have, and not to leap-upon beyond measure recklessly the things beyond, nor indeed to desire the not-yet gifted to them, thinking common and walkable for the many what are administered by nods from above alone for those.
translator_notes: Section ends complete before §10 order theme.

title: Unconfused sacred order; Lord the portion; no land lot for Levi
english: Palladius: You spoke well.
Cyril: So then in the unconfused order are the sacred things; for thus it would be fitting, and not to have otherwise.
Palladius: You speak well.

Cyril: And as it were a common lot he apportions to both, the gift-bearings of those under hand, and as many as one should bring up unto a dedication and sacrifice to God, these he says must be of priests and Levites together. For thus the God of the wholes said toward Aaron: ‘In their land you will not inherit, and a portion will not be for you in them; because I am your portion and your inheritance in midst of the sons of Israel. And to the sons of Levi: Behold I have given every tenth in Israel in a lot instead of their liturgies, as many as they themselves liturgize a liturgy in the tent of the witness, and the sons of Israel will no longer come forward into the tent of the witness to take a death-bearing sin, and the Levite himself will liturgize the liturgy of the tent of the witness, and they themselves will take their sins; eternal lawful into their generations, and in midst of sons of Israel they will not inherit an inheritance; because the tenths of the sons of Israel as many as if they should set apart to Lord, a taking-away I have given to the Levites in a lot; through this I have said to them: In midst of sons of Israel they will not inherit a lot.’ And in Deuteronomy at least having as it were cycled the same word, somehow thus he says: ‘There will not be for the priests the Levites, for whole tribe of Levi, a portion, nor a lot with Israel. Fruits of Lord their lot; they will eat them. And a lot will not be for them in their brothers; Lord himself his lot, according as he said to him. And this the judgment of the priests the things from the people from those sacrificing the victims, whether a calf, or a sheep; and you will give the arm to the priest, and the jaws, and the fourth-stomach, and the firstfruits of your grain, and of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstfruit of the shearings of your sheep you will give him; because Lord chose him from all your tribes, to stand before Lord the God, to liturgize and to bless upon his name, he and his sons all the days.’ So then observe how unarranged with the people is the sacred race, and somehow has been marked-off from the others; and not only by the practices according to the liturgy, but already also by the difference of the hope. For for those living through the earth-fallen life, and having clung to the earthly and thirsted the temporary, and driving past in equal to shadows, it would reasonably be said: ‘This is your portion, this your lot, a portion of your disobeying me, says Lord.’ And for those having prized the holy and blameless life, and already chosen-out through virtue, very well must be said: ‘In their land you will not inherit, and a portion will not be for you in them; because I am your portion and your inheritance,’
translator_notes: Ends mid κληρονομία σου, into next slice; PG mid-cut kept.
